title: The Dark Fantastic
summary: The world of the Sorcerers Crusade.

claims.text: History here bends on purpose: with history itself changing, exact dates matter less; if Joan of Arc escapes the fire, the date of the burning no longer matters.
It is also a secret history, much of it forgotten, hidden or destroyed in the five centuries that follow.
Each magickal culture has its own words; the glossary gives only the terms magi share across the known world.

title: The Council of the Nine Mystick Traditions
summary: The new fellowship of mystick magi.

claims.text: The Council, or the Traditions, is a fellowship just forming among mysticks who want to keep the old ways of magick and follow the Path of Gold.
Disparate is an insult for magi who will not take sides, and the name of groups that came to the Council but never joined.
Horizon is the border of God's Earth and Heaven, and the name of a vast Realm where the Traditions meet.
Mysticks is a general name for magi who work open magick rather than science-magick.
The Order of Reason is an international league of philosopher-scientists who reject magick for science and reason and seek Enlightenment for all humanity.
Daedalean is a catch-all word for its members, after the Greek inventor Daedalus, one of the Order's patron saints.
A philosopher-scientist weaves effects from formulae and science and seldom calls it magick.
Artisans, capitalised, are magi who work through machines or sacred geometry.

title: The Paths of Gold, Thorns and Screams
summary: The three roads a sorcerer may walk.

claims.text: The Path of Gold is the road to Ascension, a state beyond power and limit, admired by many and walked by few.
The Path of Thorns is the wizard's lot: a winding climb through temptation and blindness, in hope of the Zenith or the Path of Gold.
The Path of Screams is the road of Infernalists and Marauds, toward a debased or demented state.
Hubris is the deadly pride that ruins most sorcerers and those near them; the Fall is the loss of ideals, usually through Infernalism or Hubris.

title: Casual and Vain Magick
summary: How belief decides what magick the age allows.

claims.text: Casual magick is the subtle kind and vain, or vulgar, magick the open kind; the Scourge is the price of magick.
Magick is believable if it comes through accepted practice: a magus whose rites fit local belief can fly or change shape without offence.
The line moves by time and by place: new ideas shift it fast, and a stranger's magick is vain, so a European's Arts may be vain in distant lands.
Casual magick calls on divine or demonic favour, looks like an accident, uses prepared tools or takes time to prepare; anything inside medieval folklore should be casual.
Difficulty is the highest Sphere plus 3 for casual, plus 4 for vain with no Sleeper present, plus 5 for vain with witnesses.

title: The Scourge
summary: Fortune that rises to strike or bless a sorcerer.

claims.text: The Scourge is fortune, good or bad, that surrounds every sorcerer and at times rises to strike; some see it as God's punishment for altering Creation.
Any vain Effect earns a point of Scourge, even when it works.
Each Arete roll adds a Fortune Die: a 1 on it is a Bane, a 10 a Boon, and either one spends the whole Scourge pool. One more Fortune Die is added per 5 points in the pool.
To clear it, a magus meditates alone at least one day for each point in the pool.

title: Otherworlds of the Age
summary: The spirit lands as magi of the Renaissance name them.

claims.text: Otherworlds are the spirit lands beyond the Common World: Heavens, Hells, elemental courts and stranger Realms.
The Contrarium is Heaven's dark mirror below the Earth's crust, holding Purgatory, the true Hells and the Shadowlands.
The Aethyrs are realms of higher awareness around the Earth; the Void, or Abyss, is the endless space around Creation, later the Deep Umbra.
The Gauntlet is the cold threshold between Matter and Spirit; the Penumbra lies just beyond it. Umbra is an uncommon word here.
The Mist is the blindness most mortals live in, and the fog around the spirit worlds; Moonpaths are bridges through it guarded by moon spirits.
A Shallowing is a time or place where worlds overlap and a normal person could cross. Fragmenti and Vada are realms later called Shard and Shade Realms.
The Daemon is the mystick self that wakes at Awakening, later called the Avatar.
A consor is an unawakened associate with some rare talent; grog is a slighting word for a servant; an acolyte serves a magus from religious duty.
A covenant is a Hermetic stronghold, or any settled magickal community. A cray is a wellspring where Creation's power pools.
Quintessence is the fifth essence through all Creation, also called Prima, Vis or Earth's Blood; tass is Quintessence in solid form.
The Trinity is change, order and decay together keeping Creation in motion.
Fate, Fortune or Free Will is a great debate of the age, and all three play a part in magick.
The Ahl-i-Batin, or Batini, are Arabian mystics who weave the Web of Faith and seek unity for all.

title: Akashic Brotherhood
summary: Mind and body masters from far lands.

claims.text: The Akashic Brotherhood are visitors from distant lands with fearsome arts of mind and combat.

title: Chakravanti
summary: Mystics of the Wheel of death and rebirth.

claims.text: The Chakravanti, also called Euthanatoi, are forbidding mystics who ride the Wheel of death and rebirth.
The Choeur Celeste, or Celestial Chorus, are Christian heretics bound together by God's song and the call of a wider faith.
The Dream-speakers are shamans from lands unknown to Europe, joined by their insight into the ways of spirits.

title: Order of Hermes
summary: Proud wizards of protocol and Art.

claims.text: The Order of Hermes are proud wizards with elaborate rules of conduct and mighty Arts.
Umbrood, meaning shadow-children, is the Hermetic word for spirits of every kind.
The Seers of Chronos, or Sahajiya, are strange visionaries known for carnal appetites and prophecies beyond the ordinary.
The Solificati are wealthy alchemists who pursue the Great Art of refining base matter into perfect spirit.
The Verbena are witches, both hunters and hunted, who keep their Pagan faiths alive.
The Artificers, also called Dalou'lanshi, are master craftsmen joined by mechanical invention.
The Cabal of Pure Thought, or Gabrielites, are true believers working for one world under God.
The Celestial Masters, later known as Copernicans, chart and explore the heavens and what lies past them.
They call their voyages into the Void In Profundum Expeditio, a journey into the endless.
The Craftmasons, also Lion Brothers or simply Masons, are hard workers with old secrets and iron will.
The High Guild, Grand Financiers or Guildsmen, hold that nothing happens without money, and they make things happen.
The Hippocratic Circle, or Cosians, master the healing arts and living flesh.
The Void Seekers, or Explorators, are explorers with their eyes on the eternal horizon.
A Skyrigger is a ship built to fly into the Heavens, and also the name for those who sail one.

title: Ksirafai
summary: The Razors who do not exist.

claims.text: The Ksirafai are not counted among the Conventions; called Razors, they stay unknown even within the Order.
They are intriguers who set the Order's plans in motion.

title: Ranks and Words of the Order
summary: The Order of Reason's own vocabulary.

claims.text: Brethren are the unenlightened companions and servants of the Order; a Mediator has reached Enlightenment but not yet mastered the Ars Praeclarus.
A Resplendent works the craft others call magick; a Magistrate is a ranking member; a Resplendent Honestus is high-born and high-ranked.
Each Convention has two Resplendent Maximi, one man and one woman, who sit for it on the Inner Circle, the Order's ruling council.
A Guildhall is a Convention's chief lodge; a Lodge is a Daedalean covenant and workshop; a Machina is a powerful device; Viasilicos are crystals for talking between distant lodges.
Enlightenment is the Order's word for Awakening; in theory anyone could reach it once plague, monsters and oppression are lifted.
The Primi, the First, are the ten founders of the Council and the speakers for each group.
Promethian is a back-handed name for a member of the Order of Reason; Squama, after armour plates, is a plain insult for Daedaleans.
A Mastiga is a foolish apprentice, a young and stupid magus or a careless censor.
Order members call mysticks Superstitionists, and call night-folk and rival magi Dolores.
The Disparate are independent magi who walk their own Paths rather than join the Council or the Order.

title: Making a Magus
summary: The steps for a Sorcerers Crusade character.

claims.text: Choose concept, society, Essence, Nature and Demeanor, and settle the style of magick, beliefs and history.
Attributes are ranked 7, 5 and 3; Abilities 13, 9 and 5, none above 3 at this stage.
Advantages are 7 Background dots and 6 Sphere dots; Arete starts at 1, Willpower at 5, and there are 15 freebie points.

title: Essences of the Age
summary: The four kinds of mystick soul.

claims.text: Castellum souls are fortresses of order that slay dragons within and without; Furo souls are fiery and seek the divine in chaos.
Mare souls are deep as the sea, rooted in nature and eternity; Sussuro souls are laughing winds on an endless quest.

title: The Nine Spheres
summary: The parts of Creation a magus can master.

claims.text: Connection covers ties between people and places; Entropy, fate, fortune and decay; Forces, the elements.
Life gives insight into living things, Matter into solid material, and Mind into thought.
Prime commands Quintessence; Spirit covers the spirit world and its dwellers; Time covers past, present, future and the roads between.
An Affinity Sphere is the element tied to a magus's personality and Awakening; Arete, the trait rolled to cast, measures enlightened will.
Arcane hides a magus from notice; Covenant is the cabal's meeting place or fellowship; Cray is a nearby wellspring of Quintessence.
Daemon rates the power and personality of the mystick self; Destiny marks those fated for great deeds or great deaths.
Others include Allies, Familiar, Influence, Library, Magickal Treasure, Mentor, Resources, Sanctum and Spies.
The basic list includes Artist, Instruction, Archery, Riding, Academics, Enigmas, Lore, Metaphysics and Occult.
Secondary Abilities include Dancing, Intrigue, Invention, Logic, Artillerist, Do, Fencing, Firearms, Torture, Cosmology, Hearth Wisdom, Herbalism, Moneylending, Poisons and Secret Code Language.

title: True Faith and Echoes
summary: A pious Merit and a folkloric Flaw.

claims.text: True Faith is a Merit of 7 points or more that lets the pious work miracles.
Echoes is a Flaw worth 1 to 5 freebie points: folklore can and does hurt the magus.
